what: The quantising rule of spec/undertone.toml on small sets: scale the set so its largest magnitude maps to 2^17 - 1 = 131071, then round half to even. Every expected value in 'cases' was worked BY HAND, and the working is in each case's 'worked' lines. The reference pulse's 64 coefficients, in 'e0', were worked by code that imports nothing of model/ (tests/test_mod_b_weights.py recomputes them the same way at every run: round half up by integers, which equals round half to even because the set has no exact tie, and the test asserts that it has none), and four of them by hand.
format: A value is an integer, or [numerator, denominator] for a fraction.

cases.name: peaks
worked: the largest magnitude is 1, so each value is multiplied by 131071: 131071, -131071, 0. The rule never gives -131072.

cases.name: halves
worked: the largest magnitude is 262142 = 2 * 131071, so each value v scales to v / 2
1 -> 0.5, a tie between 0 and 1: the even one is 0
half away from zero would give 1, 2, 3, -1, -2, -3 for the six small values; half up would give 1, 2, 3, 0, -1, -2

cases.name: ties-far-from-zero
worked: each value v scales to v / 2

cases.name: quarters
worked: the largest magnitude is 4, so each value v scales to v * 131071 / 4

cases.name: fractions
worked: the largest magnitude is 1/3, so each value v scales to 3 * v * 131071

cases.name: four-samples-of-the-reference-pulse
worked: the largest magnitude is 970, the reference pulse's own

e0.worked: v * 131071 / 970 for each of spec.constants.PULSES['e0'], in order, to the nearest integer. No value is an exact tie: 131071 is prime, so a tie needs a sample of 485 or -485, and the pulse has none.
